title: Fitbit won't charge on proprietary cable
shortDescription: Device not recognizing charger, no charge indicator.
fullDescription: Fitbit chargers are model-specific and pogo-pin based. Failures trace to debris between pins and contacts, a loose fit, or a failed cable. Wipe contacts with isopropyl, align magnets (if applicable), and try a different USB port with ≥500 mA output.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe Fitbit and cable pins with isopropyl.

fixSteps.title: Try different port
fixSteps.instruction: Use 5V/1A+ wall adapter or computer USB 3.0.

fixSteps.title: Replace cable
fixSteps.instruction: Order OEM Fitbit charger if cable damaged.

title: Fitbit won't connect to Fitbit app
shortDescription: App cannot discover or maintain link to device.
fullDescription: Connection failures usually trace to Bluetooth, permission, or stale pairing problems. Toggle Bluetooth on phone, ensure location permission is granted, and remove/re-add device in the Fitbit app if needed.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Off/on on phone; restart phone if needed.

fixSteps.title: Grant permissions
fixSteps.instruction: Bluetooth, Nearby Devices, Location for Fitbit app.

videoSearchQuery: Fitbit won't connect to app fix

title: Fitbit sync fails
shortDescription: App pulls partial data or fails to update.
fullDescription: Sync failures often follow an OS update that changes Bluetooth behavior or a Google/Fitbit account migration. Restart the device (hold button 10s), force-close app, and retry. If persistent, check account migration status at fitbit.com.

fixSteps.title: Restart Fitbit
fixSteps.instruction: Hold button 10s or follow model restart steps.

fixSteps.title: Update app/OS
fixSteps.instruction: Update both Fitbit app and phone OS.

title: Fitbit heart rate not detecting
shortDescription: HR complication shows dashes or no reading.
fullDescription: Optical sensor requires firm skin contact. Wear the band snug, two finger widths above wrist bone during workouts. Ensure the Heart Rate setting is On in device settings.

fixSteps.title: Tighten + position
fixSteps.instruction: Two fingers above wrist bone, snug but comfortable.

videoSearchQuery: Fitbit heart rate not working fix

title: Fitbit stuck on logo at boot
shortDescription: Device never progresses past logo after restart.
fullDescription: A stuck logo typically follows a failed firmware update. Keep device on charger and perform model-specific restart (hold button(s) 10-15s). If unresolved, contact Fitbit support — some models support recovery via the Fitbit app.

fixSteps.title: Contact Fitbit
fixSteps.instruction: Fitbit support may push recovery firmware.

title: Fitbit touchscreen unresponsive
shortDescription: Screen wakes but taps and swipes do nothing.
fullDescription: Moisture and screen protectors frequently disable Fitbit touch. Dry the screen, remove any protector, and restart the device. Persistent touch failures may indicate digitizer damage.

fixSteps.title: Dry + remove protector
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe screen, remove screen protector if present.

title: Fitbit battery drains in hours
shortDescription: Battery life much shorter than advertised.
fullDescription: Rapid drain often follows a firmware update or comes from continuous GPS, always-on display, or a buggy app. Disable always-on, reduce notifications, and restart the device.

title: Fitbit GPS fails to acquire
shortDescription: Built-in or connected GPS unavailable at workout start.
fullDescription: Built-in GPS (Charge 5/6, Versa 4, Sense 2) needs clear sky. Phone-connected GPS (older models) needs app permissions. Sync to refresh satellite data before workouts.

fixSteps.title: Sync
fixSteps.instruction: Sync Fitbit to refresh GPS assist data.

title: Fitbit alarms stopped triggering
shortDescription: Alarm vibration does not occur despite alarms set.
fullDescription: Alarms are synced from Fitbit app but require Do Not Disturb to be off and the device worn. After account migration or firmware update, alarms may need to be resynced.

fixSteps.title: Re-sync alarms
fixSteps.instruction: Fitbit app > Alarms > toggle off/on; sync.

title: Fitbit band causing skin irritation
shortDescription: Redness or rash under the band area.
fullDescription: Trapped moisture, soap residue, and too-tight fit cause contact dermatitis. Clean band and wrist daily, loosen fit, and rotate wrist position. Switch to a breathable band (nylon/mesh) for sensitive skin.

fixSteps.title: Loosen + dry
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen one hole; dry wrist and band after workouts.

fixSteps.title: Clean daily
fixSteps.instruction: Wash with gentle soap, rinse, dry before rewearing.
